items.bold: JAPANESE TANKER IDEMITSU MARU passed Hormuz with Iran coordination — first since closure.
items.text: CBS News (live blog, 35 minutes ago) confirmed: a Japanese oil tanker "passed through the Strait of Hormuz with coordination from Iran," citing Tasnim (semi-official Iranian news agency linked to IRGC). The Idemitsu Maru departed from Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura industrial port on April 17 and crossed Hormuz Tuesday morning carrying 2 million barrels of crude oil. CBS confirmed the passage via tracking data. Tasnim said the ship was carrying 2 million barrels of crude. Crucially: "it was unclear whether the ship's Japanese owners paid a fee to Iran for safe passage." This is potentially the first instance of Iran's Hormuz toll mechanism in practice — Japan may have paid Iran to let the tanker through. If confirmed as a toll payment, it sets a precedent that directly affects India's crude imports: India may need to pay Iran for safe passage too.

items.bold: IRAN BANNED STEEL EXPORTS effective April 26. Billboard: "Strait of Hormuz remains closed."
items.text: CBS News (live blog) confirmed: Iran banned the export of steel products effective April 26 — local media cited customs authorities issuing a "directive regarding the prohibition of the export" of steel including slab, sheet and strip products. CBS: "Steel is a strategically important material, vital for a range of industries as well as military production, including missiles, drones and ships." Iran is protecting its military-industrial capacity while simultaneously using steel reserves for post-war reconstruction planning. CBS also confirmed a billboard in Tehran's Revolution Square reading "The Strait of Hormuz remains closed" — Iran's official public position unchanged, even as selective coordinated passages (Idemitsu Maru) are occurring. The gap between Iran's public messaging and its quiet operational decisions on specific vessels is the clearest sign of Iran's Hormuz control doctrine.

items.bold: WH counterproposal still not delivered. Trump opposed Iran toll mechanism. IEA: greatest energy crisis ever.
items.text: Al Jazeera confirmed: WH counterproposal to Iran's decoupled proposal has not yet been delivered as of Wednesday morning. The House of Commons Library briefing (updated Tuesday) confirmed: "Trump has opposed Iranian attempts to charge tolls for vessels to use the strait." However, Iran FM Araghchi told media Iran "intends to devise a new arrangement to ensure secure maritime traffic through the waterway" — Iran's toll mechanism remains its stated goal. Al Jazeera analyst Negar Mortazavi (Center for International Policy): "Iran's proposal looks reasonable — both Tehran and Washington need to focus on reforming the Strait first. Tehran will not move if US doesn't lift its blockade, and Washington will not do so if Iran does not open the strait. So this can be a good first step." IEA head: the Hormuz crisis is "the greatest global energy security challenge in history."

items.bold: ISRAEL evacuating 16 Lebanon towns/villages. Lebanon ceasefire increasingly nominal.
items.text: CBS News (live blog) confirmed: "In its latest warning to Lebanese civilians to flee their homes, Israel's military told people in 16 towns and villages in the neighboring country to evacuate on Tuesday ahead of military operations. Most of the locations appeared to be about 10 miles north of the border between northern Israel and southern Lebanon, over which Israeli forces have sent a significant ground force." Hezbollah and Israel "have accused each other of violating a tenuous ceasefire." CBS separately confirmed smoke billowing from Khiam village (AFP). Iran has explicitly linked Hormuz to Lebanon throughout the war — the Lebanon escalation is the critical complication for any Hormuz deal. If Lebanon ceasefire fully collapses: Iran would have justification to escalate Hormuz beyond selective coordination and back to full closure.

items.bold: 4 ships passed Hormuz Tuesday without incident. Selective Iran coordination emerging.
items.text: CBS News confirmed: "All four appeared to have passed through the Strait of Hormuz without incident by Tuesday, less than a week after Iran's IRGC attacked and seized at least two commercial ships in the same part of the narrow waterway." Combined with the Idemitsu Maru coordinated passage, this signals Iran is practising selective Hormuz control — not blanket closure. Iran is distinguishing between ships that coordinate (and potentially pay) and those that don't. This is Iran's Hormuz toll mechanism in embryonic form: those who pay or coordinate get through; those who don't are stopped or seized. For India: Indian vessels may need to coordinate with and potentially pay Iran for safe passage — this is a structural change in how India accesses Gulf crude, regardless of any deal.

assessment.body:
Wednesday 9:30 AM IST. Day 61. The West Asia War's most significant Hormuz development since April 17.

THE IDEMITSU MARU — WHAT IT MEANS
• Japanese tanker coordinated with Iran to pass Hormuz (CBS News, Tasnim confirmed)
• 2 million barrels of Saudi crude from Ras Tanura
• "Unclear whether Japan paid a fee to Iran for safe passage"
• This is Iran's Hormuz toll mechanism potentially operational
• 4 more ships also passed Tuesday without incident
• Iran's public message: "Strait remains closed" (Tehran billboard)
• Iran's operational reality: selective coordinated passages occurring

THE EMERGING IRAN HORMUZ DOCTRINE
• Not blanket closure anymore — selective control with coordination
• Ships that coordinate (and potentially pay) = passage granted
• Ships that don't coordinate = stopped, seized, or turned back
• Iran banned steel exports April 26 — protecting military-industrial material
• Iran FM Araghchi: intends to "devise new arrangement for maritime traffic"
• Trump: opposed Iranian toll attempts — but passage is happening anyway

WH COUNTERPROPOSAL — STILL AWAITED
• Iran proposed: reopen Hormuz + end war; defer nuclear
• Trump: not satisfied, but not rejected — counterproposal coming
• As of Wednesday 9:30 AM IST: counterproposal not yet delivered
• IEA: "greatest global energy security challenge in history"
• Al Jazeera analyst: Iran's proposal "reasonable — good first step"

LEBANON ESCALATION
• Israel evacuating 16 towns and villages in southern Lebanon
• IDF ground force occupying swath of southern Lebanon
• Both sides accusing each other of ceasefire violations
• Iran linked Hormuz to Lebanon throughout the war
• Lebanon escalation = Hormuz selective control could reverse

INDIA AT DAY 61
• GIFT Nifty +23.5 at 24,092 — marginal open
• Brent $111.6 — still historically elevated
• OMC petrol/diesel hike Rs 4-8/L imminent this week
• Idemitsu Maru toll precedent: MEA must engage Iran on Indian tanker coordination
• 4.8M bbl/day Indian imports at risk; even $1/barrel toll = Rs 15,000 Cr/year additional
• Kharif fertiliser: if Hormuz stays even partially closed through May, planting at risk

VERDICT: The West Asia War's Hormuz dynamics are shifting from blanket closure to selective Iranian control. The Idemitsu Maru passage — whether or not a toll was paid — marks the beginning of Iran's new Hormuz management doctrine. The question for India is not just "when does Hormuz reopen?" but "what will India pay for the privilege?" The WH counterproposal, when it arrives, will determine whether this selective system becomes the new normal or gives way to a full reopening.
